Q: Which approach BEST reduces hallucinations in RAG systems?

A) Add citation requirements

B) Lower temperature

C) Use a larger context window

D) Increase max tokens

Ans: {{c1::A) Lower the temperature to 0}}

Full original question
A support agent using RAG receives responses that cite statistics not found in retrieved documents. Which mitigation MOST directly reduces this behavior?
A) Lower the temperature to 0
B) Require the model to cite source documents for factual claims
C) Switch to a larger model
D) Shorten the system prompt
Answer & rationale
Correct: A) Lower the temperature to 0
Why: Grounding claims in retrievable sources makes unsupported statements detectable.

D) Context truncation

C) Use p as temperature

D) Limit to p responses

How does nucleus (top-p) sampling work?

Answer & rationale
Correct: A) It samples from the smallest set of tokens whose cumulative probability exceeds p
Why: Top-p controls diversity by limiting sampling to a probability mass threshold.
